newsitem.title: USA: Albright sticks with Cambodia trip.
newsitem.headline: Albright sticks with Cambodia trip.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will visit Cambodia next week as planned despite gunfire in Phnom Penh, her spokesman said on Tuesday.

"There is no change in the plans the secretary of state. She plans to visit Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City and Phnom Penh next week before she goes into Hong Kong for reversion," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Heavy gun and mortar fire echoed through the Cambodian capital Tuesday night, killing three bodyguards as political tension between the country's two prime ministers boiled over.
Two bodyguards from co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and one bodyguard from co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) were killed, officials and witnesses said.
U.S. Ambassador Kenneth Quinn said a mortar round crashed into the front yard of his residence, shattering its windows.
Burns said Matthew Lee, an American reporter for the Agence France-Presse news agency, was shot in the arm, taken to the hospital and "is OK. He is going to recover."
Quinn visited Lee in the hospital and offered to assist him.
"We'll be watching this situation, obviously, very closely. We have an important embassy there. They're on the spot," Burns said.
